source.description: Discovery channel. Always "web" in v3 — the only allowed value. Mirrors agent.providers.source.

source_id.description: Optional stable id from the discovery channel, kept for cheap traceability. For web discovery there is usually none, so emit null. Use a non-empty string ONLY when the channel exposes a stable identifier. The key MUST be present even when null. Mirrors agent.providers.source_id.

name.description: Provider / store display name as shown on its own website (e.g. "Leyva Scents"). Mirrors agent.providers.name.

catalog_url.description: URL of the provider's own catalog / storefront. REQUIRED — a provider with no own functional website fails the hard gate and must not be emitted at all. Mirrors agent.providers.catalog_url (NOT NULL in v3).

whatsapp.description: Contact phone / WhatsApp as digits. Emit JSON null when the site exposes no phone — NEVER an empty string, "N/A", "no disponible", "-", or any placeholder. A sentinel string is not recognized as empty downstream and would corrupt the dedup hash. The key MUST be present even when null. Mirrors agent.providers.whatsapp.

instagram_handle.description: Instagram handle WITHOUT the leading "@". Emit JSON null when there is none — NEVER an empty string or placeholder (same dedup-corruption reason as whatsapp). The key MUST be present even when null. Mirrors agent.providers.instagram_handle.

evidence_urls.description: Flat list of URLs justifying why this provider was admitted (catalog / about / shipping / returns / policy pages). Populate it: an empty array does not meet the evidence standard. Do NOT fabricate a URL to fill it — if you genuinely have none, emit the honest empty array; the deterministic validateAndFilter (sprint 2R.3) rejects empty evidence, not this schema. Mirrors agent.providers.evidence_urls.

discovery_query.description: The exact web_search query that surfaced this provider. Mirrors agent.providers.discovery_query.

confidence.description: How sure the model is of its OWN trust_quality judgement, given the coverage and quality of accessible evidence — NOT enthusiasm about the store. Distinct axis from trust_quality (see system prompt §5.3): a legitimate store with thin evidence is high trust_quality / low confidence; a mediocre store seen in full is low trust_quality / high confidence. Be honest — do not inflate to clear any downstream threshold; the deterministic filter (2R.3) applies the cut, not you.

trust_quality.description: Substantive judgement of the provider's legitimacy and premium fit, in [0,1]. Raised by: real visible contact, demonstrable age, a deep structured catalog, site/socials consistency, transactional signals (cart, payment methods, shipping/returns policy), carrying REFERENCE_BRANDS_V3 houses. Lowered by: full bottles only (no decants), tiny/generic catalog, no verifiable contact, uncurated dropshipper signals, IMPOSSIBLY LOW PRICES (counterfeit signal), cross-channel inconsistency. Geography modulates this (see §5.4) — there is no geography field. Emit the raw honest score, including below any threshold. Mirrors agent.providers.trust_quality.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Default and expected value is "active". Emit "inactive" or "suspended" ONLY with explicit evidence in evidence_urls (e.g. dead domain, a "cerramos" notice, long-dormant socials) — never on a hunch. Mirrors agent.providers.status.

providers.description: Up to 30 decants providers discovered this run (PROVIDERS_MAX_PER_RUN). May be empty. Contains ONLY the fields the model has an epistemic basis to produce. trust_fulfillment, last_verified_at, dedup_hash, id and run_id are injected by the workflow Code node before the ProviderSchema (v3) parse / UPSERT and are deliberately absent here.
